addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- docs-consistency-guard: Documentation agent that audits docs for staleness and inconsistency AND generates/updates documentation on request. Use proactively when reviewing any PR that touches CLAUDE.md, docs/adr/, CONTRIBUTING.md, or docs/architecture.md. Also invoke when the user asks "is the documentation up to date?", "update the milestone", "scaffold the ADR for X", "add this to the ADR index", "add a TODO item", "scaffold a README for X", or "create a doc stub for Y." (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit)

- driver-boundary-guard: Specialized reviewer for values that cross a DRIVER boundary — anything DataQ receives from a database connector, pyiceberg, pandas/pyarrow, or a cloud SDK and then type-narrows (isinstance / dtype checks / hasattr). Audits whether the covering tests hand-build the value in the shape our model expects (the "fixture encodes our model" defect that hid (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- migration-safety: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- orchestration-abstraction-guard: Specialized reviewer that audits backend code for provider-specific branching that bypasses the OrchestrationProvider abstraction. Use this proactively when reviewing any PR that touches backend/app/orchestration/, backend/app/services/, or backend/app/api/ — especially any code path handling ADF or Airflow events, trigger bindings, or pipeline_runs. Also invoke when the user asks "does this go through the abstraction?" or similar. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- qa-verifier: QA/QE agent that (1) runs the full local verification battery mirroring CI's required checks before any commit/push/PR, (2) audits test quality on changed code — failure-mode coverage, mocked-seam smells, coverage on changed files (Week-8 ≥80% gate), and (3) exercises the running application with data-level scenarios — authoring suites/checks through the real API, negative and edge-case inputs, authz probes — against the local stack's seeded demo data. Use proactively before pushing a branch or opening a PR, after writing or modifying tests, or when the user asks "run the gate", "is this ready to push?", "is this tested enough?", or "smoke the app with bad data". (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- regression-mutation-verifier: Proves that a new regression test actually fails against the unfixed code. Reverts the fix inside a throwaway git worktree, runs only the new test, and reports whether it fails for the RIGHT reason — catching tests that pass no matter what (the (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Edit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- ui-tester: End-to-end UI QA agent that exercises DataQ's frontend on BOTH desktop and mobile viewports (functionality + rendering) against the running app, AND audits backend↔frontend feature parity — flagging backend capabilities with no frontend surface (and frontend calls with no backend). Use when the user asks to "test the UI", "check mobile rendering", "find backend/frontend gaps", "is this feature wired end-to-end", or before a release. Drives a live browser via the Playwright MCP and reads code for the parity audit. (Tools: All tools)

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

anomaly monitor kind — metric_value baseline/seasonality model
----
Theme 1 / gap G-a (post-v1-roadmap) — the second reserved kind (ADR 0012), and the one that needs a model: learn a baseline from a check's own `metric_value` history (the SQL-aggregatable scalar was designed for exactly this) and flag runs that deviate.

**Scope:**
- **v1 of the model: deliberately simple + explainable** — rolling window mean/stddev (z-score) with optional day-of-week seasonality; no ML dependency. Persist the baseline via the shape designed in #592 (schema_drift lands it first).
- `metric_value` on the anomaly result = the deviation score; band it through the existing ADR 0016 thresholds so warn/fail/critical need no new severity machinery.
- Cold-start handling: below N historical points → `skip` status (exists since #297/#298), never a fake pass/fail.
- Authoring UI variant (window size, sensitivity, target metric — e.g. anomaly *on* a volume monitor's row count).
- Pairs with the per-check metric-trend view (#594) — same week so the trend chart can draw the learned band, which is also how you visually debug the model.

This + #592 is the G-a answer at the detection layer; auto-*suggested* checks (Theme 2 LLM work) stay backlog.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rolling-window mean/stddev z-score baseline (optional day-of-week seasonality), persisted via the #592 baseline shape
- [ ] `metric_value` = deviation score, banded through existing ADR-0016 thresholds
- [ ] Cold start (< N points) yields `skip`, never a synthetic pass/fail
- [ ] Authoring UI: window size, sensitivity, target metric; E2E on local data

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_

(2) `refresh_lineage_pull` **purges** orphaned pulled edges when `LINEAGE_PROVIDER` is unset (sweep-not-badge disposition; set-but-broken keeps the cache — one typo must not become data loss). (3) **API-side workspace dead-poll alert**: `max(last_polled_at)` over all orchestration connections vs `POLL_STALENESS_ALERT_AFTER_S` (default 1800s), via the `HealthPublisher` seam + the #843 delivered-first rule on the new `workspace_health` table (additive migration). The review's big catch: **unconfigured channels counted as delivered** — the composite now raises when nothing was sent, so a fresh install can never stamp a phantom delivery; pre-existing sibling defect filed [#1101](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1101), engine `connect_timeout` gap filed [#1102](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1102) | reliability / #905 class |

Root cause **confirmed live in App Insights**: `dispatch_due_schedules` ~6,959 executions/11d while `refresh_warehouse_lineage` last ran 2026-07-18 19:15 (matching the DB's frozen `last_seen` to the minute) and `sweep_orphan_secrets` had **never run once**; the only daily task that executed was the one #1024 kicks on beat start — ≥4 beat restarts in 36h. Fix: staggered UTC crontabs (01:17–02:57) + two class-level guards (no beat entry may use an interval a restart can starve; no midnight herd; every entry names a registered task). Mutation-checked | reliability / #905 class |
| ✅ | [#1098](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1098) **Doubled "(optional)" label** (`Fixes #1066`) — `ConfigTextField`/`SecretField` manually appended `(optional)` while the enclosing forms' antd `requiredMark="optional"` already renders the marker (a #350 leftover: the manual suffix predates `requiredMark`, correct when written). Dropped the suffix, matching `PassphraseField`'s existing pattern; regression test verified to FAIL pre-fix. The same-shaped suffix in `checkFormFields.tsx` is **load-bearing** (those forms lack `requiredMark`) and deliberately untouched per #1066's own scoping | frontend / P3 |
| ✅ | [#1097](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1097) **Dead `_FLATFILE_TYPES` global removed** (CodeQL alert #64) — orphaned by #1049, which moved target-shape dispatch into the registry and cleaned the sibling dead global but missed this one | backend hygiene |
| ✅ | [#1096](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1096) **Worker-lost run closure** (`Closes #755`) — when the OOM killer SIGKILLs a prefork child mid-`run_suite`, *nothing inside the task executes* (no `except`, no `finally`), so the run sat `running` until the stuck-run reaper caught it up to 60 min later with a reason that could only say "did not complete in time". Celery's parent process already knows via the `task_failure` signal — `fail_run_worker_lost()` now closes the run immediately (idempotent, non-clobbering: terminal/cancelled runs are left alone), names memory as the likely cause, and emits the terminal OpenLineage event a `running` run would otherwise dangle. Covers 3 of #755's 4 asks; the size-probe half is #595's. Regression test mutation-checked after the first version passed with the task-name guard deleted | execution / P1 |
| ✅ | [#1095](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1095) **Snowflake `role` required on every connection** (`Closes #1067`) — GX's `REQUIRED_QUERY_PARAMS` is `{warehouse, role}`, so a role-less connection produced a DSN GX rejects at `add_snowflake`. The validator already encoded this reasoning but scoped it to key-pair: **the reasoning was right, the scope was wrong** — the requirement is GX's, not the auth method's. So a role-less *password* connection **tested green and failed every run** (the test is GX-free; monitors bypass GX, so it looked *partly* alive — the #828/#954 shape). **Prod checked before tightening: 3 connections, 0 role-less** — nothing to migrate. **The demo seed shipped the same defect** (2 role-less connections, found only when its test broke), and **the suite was pinning the bug** — 3 tests asserted role was optional. Now pins **GX's own** `REQUIRED_QUERY_PARAMS`, so if GX relaxes it the validator gets revisited rather than outliving its reason | datasources / P1 |
| ✅ | [#1094](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1094) **`.env.app.example` blank bool broke a fresh install** (`Closes #1072`) — `OPENLINEAGE_DISABLED=` blank is not a parseable bool, and `setup.sh` never fills it, so the documented from-scratch path produced a config the app cannot construct. One line, plus the part that matters: **two mutation-checked guard tests**, because nothing checked the shipped template was loadable. Writing them was the lesson — **two attempts asserted things the architecture deliberately denies** (`.env.example` isn't a Settings file, `extra=forbid`/#209; the RAW template isn't meant to load because secret keys ship blank by design). The assertion is *"the .env.app setup.sh produces must load"*; both exclusions are documented so nobody re-tightens them | config / P1 |

Key lives in the gitignored `terraform.tfvars` — **not `.env`**, which `scripts/setup.sh` regenerates, and regenerating it would make the state permanently unreadable. **Claim kept honest**: the key sits beside the ciphertext, so it buys little against host compromise and a lot against *accidental* disclosure (committed state, a `.tfstate.backup` swept into a backup, a state pasted into a ticket). **Rehearsed on a throwaway stack before touching prod**, which settled four assumptions — incl. that a **no-op apply still rewrites state** (decisive, our plan is clean) — and one rehearsal check was *invalid on first run* because `terraform.tfvars` outranks `TF_VAR_`, so the "wrong passphrase" never reached the block. Verified on the real stack: plan `exitcode=0`, wrong passphrase `exit 1 / cipher: message authentication failed`, re-plan `0` (uncorrupted). **This makes the ADR 0024 OpenTofu swap STRUCTURAL** — Terraform cannot parse `encryption {}`. Then the `#1090` purge check against **live prod** answered itself and found something worse: **zero `source='marquez'` edges ever existed** (configured, but its target was `Stopped`) — nothing to purge, lucky on the data rather than right by design — while `snowflake` + `unity_catalog` edges sat **9 days stale** despite the flag being on. | ✅ | [#1088](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1088) **IaC CLI Terraform → OpenTofu** (ADR [0024](adr/0024-app-deployment-infrastructure.md) amended in place, ADR [0021](adr/0021-demo-test-data-environment-strategy.md) likewise for the harness) — Terraform has been BUSL-1.1 since v1.6 and was the last source-available binary touching an MIT project. **Nothing was in violation** (rule 40 governs the *dependency tree*; the CLI never enters an image) — coherence, timed by #505 since converting one stack is contained and three is not. **A clean plan was never the bar** — the stack carries pre-existing drift — so the bar was *equivalence*: both CLIs planned against live Azure, `-out` → `show -json` → normalized `resource_changes` diffed **byte-for-byte identical** (40 changes, `no-op=38 update=2`). === #594 ===
Per-check metric-value trend view with threshold bands
Theme 9 (post-v1-roadmap, design-captured 2026-07-04) — filed now because it's scheduled into v1.1 W5.

A 'this check over time' chart of `metric_value` with the warn/fail/critical threshold bands drawn on it — the payoff view the ADR 0016/0012 scalar-metric design was built for. One lazy-loaded recharts component (ADR 0022) + a query over existing data; surface it on run-detail / check history.

**W5 tie-in:** when #593 lands, the same chart overlays the learned anomaly baseline band — one component serves both the static-threshold and learned-baseline story, and doubles as the anomaly model's visual debugger.

Include the a11y lesson already captured in Theme 3's accessibility notes: don't make color the only encoding, and provide a data-table fallback.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-check `metric_value` time-series chart with warn/fail/critical bands drawn
- [ ] Anomaly-baseline overlay renders when #593 is configured (doubles as its visual debugger)
- [ ] Non-color severity encoding + a data-table fallback (a11y); recharts lazy-loaded
- [ ] Linked from run-detail and check history

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_
=== #568 ===
Threshold ordering/sign not validated on expectation-kind checks (warn≤fail≤critical assumed, never enforced)
## Finding (qa-verifier go-live workout, 2026-07-03 — non-blocking footgun)

`derive_status` (`backend/app/services/severity.py:107`) documents the assumption *thresholds are ordered (warn ≤ fail ≤ critical)* — but `create_check`/`update_check` never enforce it for plain `kind='expectation'` checks. Inverted (90/50/10) and negative thresholds both persist as 201; the ≥-cascade then degrades to surprising severity bands rather than erroring. The freshness/volume monitor path already has exactly this guard (`validate_monitor_check`) — extend the same ordering + non-negative validation to all threshold-bearing checks (422 on violation), plus a UI hint.

_Silent authoring footgun, no crash/leak — post-v1 (Theme 10 test-hardening adjacent). Found by the qa-verifier data-level workout._

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Authoring-time validation enforces threshold ordering (direction-aware warn/fail/critical); clear 422 on violation
- [ ] Existing out-of-order rows handled (documented runtime tolerance or migration)
- [ ] Tests for both directions

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_
=== #424 ===
Run-detail sample: header says 'values redacted' even when non-PII values now surface (#417 follow-up)
After #417 (column-aware redaction) deployed, the failing-row sample correctly **surfaces** non-PII values (e.g. `line_total`: 142.8, 857.4, …). But the sample header still reads `· N rows · 100% · **values redacted**` — stale/inaccurate when values are shown.

**Fix:** the redaction state should be reflected in the label — e.g. `values shown` / `non-PII values` when surfaced, `values redacted` only when actually masked. Likely needs the API/read model to signal whether the sample was redacted (or the frontend to infer from the values), so the label matches reality.

Found verifying #417 live in prod.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sample header reflects the actual redaction state (fully / partially / not redacted) after #417
- [ ] Test covering each state

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_
=== #349 ===
Results: dedupe the runs fetch across tabs + share the date-window presets with Dashboard
Cleanup follow-ups from the /code-review of PR #347 (non-blocking).

### 1. Duplicate `listRuns` fetch across the two Results tabs
[Results.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx): both RunsTab and PipelineRunsTab independently fetch `listRuns({ limit: 200 })` (PipelineRunsTab needs it only to correlate triggered DQ runs, and re-pulls it every 30s). antd Tabs lazy-mounts panes, so it's a fresh fetch on tab switch plus the poll. Lifting the runs fetch to the parent `Results` and passing it down would fetch once and keep the two tabs consistent.

### 2. `DATE_WINDOWS` duplicates Dashboard's `RANGES`
The 24h/7d/30d trailing-window presets are defined in both [Results.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx) (`DATE_WINDOWS`) and Dashboard.tsx (`RANGES`), and already disagree on labels ('Last 7 days' vs '7d'). Extract a shared `WINDOW_PRESETS` (value → days → label) so the two surfaces can't drift.

### Note (not filed separately)
The runs list is capped at `LIST_LIMIT = 200` (pre-existing): filters and DQ-run correlation operate within the newest 200 rows, so a match/triggered-run older than that is invisible. Tracked here for awareness; real fix is server-side pagination/filtering when run volume warrants it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Runs fetched once and shared across the Results tabs; date-window presets shared with Dashboard
- [ ] No visible behavior change (tests)

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_
=== #345 ===
Results export — PDF report of an executed suite run
## Summary

Add **PDF report export** of an executed suite run, alongside the JSON + CSV export already shipped in Week 6 (Phase 1.2, `8a405e9`).

## Context

The run-detail page (`/results/:runId`) gained a download menu with **CSV + JSON** in [WEEK6_TODO Phase 1.2](../blob/main/WEEK6_TODO.md). PDF was a sibling line item on the roadmap (`docs/progress.md`: "CSV + PDF export of results") and was explicitly **deferred to backlog**:

> PDF export — **deferred to backlog** (extra dep, little gain over CSV/JSON); shipped CSV/JSON in 1.2.

This issue tracks that deferred work so it isn't silently dropped.

## Scope

- A "Download → PDF" option on the run-detail header (next to CSV/JSON).
- Render a printable run report: run meta (suite, status, triggered-by, started, duration) + per-check results table (check, expectation, severity, `metric_value`, observed).
- **No sample failing rows** in the payload (PII — same withholding as CSV/JSON, see #226).

## Open questions / cost

- Adds a client- or server-side PDF dependency (e.g. a print-stylesheet `window.print()` route vs. a JS PDF lib vs. server render). Evaluate against the `pnpm audit` + bundle-size gate before adopting a lib — a print stylesheet may discharge this with zero deps.
- Little marginal value over CSV/JSON for machine consumption; value is a shareable human-readable artifact.

Relates to #250 (JSON + CSV export).


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PDF export of an executed run: suite header, per-check status/severity/metric, redaction-policy-compliant samples
- [ ] Suite-scoped authz enforced on the export endpoint; download from run detail
- [ ] Redaction parity with the API verified

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_
=== #283 ===
Check version history — restore/revert to a previous version
Follow-up to the version-history drawer (#280, shipped via #281 backend + #282 frontend). v1 is **view-only**; this adds a **Restore** action.

### Scope
- Backend: a restore path that re-applies a chosen `CheckVersion`'s snapshot to the live check (which itself records a *new* version, so restore is auditable and reversible). Reuse `record_check_version`; gate on `edit`.
- Frontend: a "Restore this version" button per non-current row in `CheckHistoryDrawer`, with a confirm, then refresh the editor + history.

### Notes
- Out of v1 deliberately — the roadmap line was "see previous config before overwriting" (read), and restore widens scope (confirm UX, re-validation of the restored config against the current connection — e.g. custom-SQL gating per ADR 0019).
- The snapshot already carries everything needed (`name`/`expectation_type`/`config`/thresholds); `kind` is immutable so it never changes on restore.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore creates a NEW version identical to the selected historical version (history preserved, no rewrite)
- [ ] Edit-permission-gated; action available in the version-history drawer; tests

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_
=== #351 ===
Test Connection button on the New/Edit connection page (draft-connection test endpoint)
## Problem
The prototype's New-Connection **Configuration** screen has a **Test Connection** button (test before saving). The shipped app has no such button on `/connections/new` (or `/connections/:id/edit`).

Today the API can only test a **saved** connection: `POST /connections/{id}/test` reads the stored secret from the SecretStore. There is no way to probe an *unsaved* draft (the config + secret the user just typed), which is what the prototype does.

## Proposed change
**Backend** — add a draft-test endpoint that probes connectivity without persisting:
- `POST /api/v1/connections/test` taking `{ type, env?, config, secret }` → runs the existing `ConnectionAdapter` probe against the ad-hoc config/secret and returns `{ ok }` (same `ConnectionTestResult` shape).
- Reuses the adapter's existing test method; **does not** write a `connections` row or store the secret.
- Security note: a credential travels in the request body (not just the id). Keep it sync-`def`/threadpool like `/test`, never log the secret (PII redactor already covers `secret`), and gate it the same as create.

**Frontend** — add a **Test connection** button to `ConnectionForm` (create mode primarily; edit mode can reuse the saved-connection `/test`). Surface ok/failed inline like the card's health badge.

## Notes
- Surfaced during W6 Phase 4 connection-page prototype-fidelity review.
- Scope is a small backend slice + a button; can ship as its own PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test Connection works on the New/Edit page BEFORE save (draft-connection test endpoint)
- [ ] Draft secrets are not persisted by the test call; clear success/failure surface; tests

_(AC added at v1.1 planning, 2026-07-04.)_

**Fix:** the redaction state should be reflected in the label — e.g. `values shown` / `non-PII values` when surfaced, `values redacted` only when actually masked. Likely needs the API/read model to signal whether the sample was redacted (or the frontend to infer from the values), so the label matches reality.

Found verifying #417 live in prod.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sample header reflects the actual redaction state (fully / partially / not redacted) after #417
- [ ] Test covering each state

=== #349 ===
Results: dedupe the runs fetch across tabs + share the date-window presets with Dashboard
Cleanup follow-ups from the /code-review of PR #347 (non-blocking).

### 1. Duplicate `listRuns` fetch across the two Results tabs
[Results.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx): both RunsTab and PipelineRunsTab independently fetch `listRuns({ limit: 200 })` (PipelineRunsTab needs it only to correlate triggered DQ runs, and re-pulls it every 30s). antd Tabs lazy-mounts panes, so it's a fresh fetch on tab switch plus the poll. Lifting the runs fetch to the parent `Results` and passing it down would fetch once and keep the two tabs consistent.

### 2. `DATE_WINDOWS` duplicates Dashboard's `RANGES`
The 24h/7d/30d trailing-window presets are defined in both [Results.tsx](frontend/src/pages/Results.tsx) (`DATE_WINDOWS`) and Dashboard.tsx (`RANGES`), and already disagree on labels ('Last 7 days' vs '7d'). Extract a shared `WINDOW_PRESETS` (value → days → label) so the two surfaces can't drift.

### Note (not filed separately)
The runs list is capped at `LIST_LIMIT = 200` (pre-existing): filters and DQ-run correlation operate within the newest 200 rows, so a match/triggered-run older than that is invisible. Tracked here for awareness; real fix is server-side pagination/filtering when run volume warrants it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Runs fetched once and shared across the Results tabs; date-window presets shared with Dashboard
- [ ] No visible behavior change (tests)

=== #345 ===
Results export — PDF report of an executed suite run
## Summary

Add **PDF report export** of an executed suite run, alongside the JSON + CSV export already shipped in Week 6 (Phase 1.2, `8a405e9`).

## Context

The run-detail page (`/results/:runId`) gained a download menu with **CSV + JSON** in [WEEK6_TODO Phase 1.2](../blob/main/WEEK6_TODO.md). PDF was a sibling line item on the roadmap (`docs/progress.md`: "CSV + PDF export of results") and was explicitly **deferred to backlog**:

> PDF export — **deferred to backlog** (extra dep, little gain over CSV/JSON); shipped CSV/JSON in 1.2.

This issue tracks that deferred work so it isn't silently dropped.

## Scope

- A "Download → PDF" option on the run-detail header (next to CSV/JSON).
- Render a printable run report: run meta (suite, status, triggered-by, started, duration) + per-check results table (check, expectation, severity, `metric_value`, observed).
- **No sample failing rows** in the payload (PII — same withholding as CSV/JSON, see #226).

## Open questions / cost

- Adds a client- or server-side PDF dependency (e.g. a print-stylesheet `window.print()` route vs. a JS PDF lib vs. server render). Evaluate against the `pnpm audit` + bundle-size gate before adopting a lib — a print stylesheet may discharge this with zero deps.
- Little marginal value over CSV/JSON for machine consumption; value is a shareable human-readable artifact.

Relates to #250 (JSON + CSV export).


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PDF export of an executed run: suite header, per-check status/severity/metric, redaction-policy-compliant samples
- [ ] Suite-scoped authz enforced on the export endpoint; download from run detail
- [ ] Redaction parity with the API verified

=== #283 ===
Check version history — restore/revert to a previous version
Follow-up to the version-history drawer (#280, shipped via #281 backend + #282 frontend). v1 is **view-only**; this adds a **Restore** action.

### Scope
- Backend: a restore path that re-applies a chosen `CheckVersion`'s snapshot to the live check (which itself records a *new* version, so restore is auditable and reversible). Reuse `record_check_version`; gate on `edit`.
- Frontend: a "Restore this version" button per non-current row in `CheckHistoryDrawer`, with a confirm, then refresh the editor + history.

### Notes
- Out of v1 deliberately — the roadmap line was "see previous config before overwriting" (read), and restore widens scope (confirm UX, re-validation of the restored config against the current connection — e.g. custom-SQL gating per ADR 0019).
- The snapshot already carries everything needed (`name`/`expectation_type`/`config`/thresholds); `kind` is immutable so it never changes on restore.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore creates a NEW version identical to the selected historical version (history preserved, no rewrite)
- [ ] Edit-permission-gated; action available in the version-history drawer; tests

=== #351 ===
Test Connection button on the New/Edit connection page (draft-connection test endpoint)
## Problem
The prototype's New-Connection **Configuration** screen has a **Test Connection** button (test before saving). The shipped app has no such button on `/connections/new` (or `/connections/:id/edit`).

Today the API can only test a **saved** connection: `POST /connections/{id}/test` reads the stored secret from the SecretStore. There is no way to probe an *unsaved* draft (the config + secret the user just typed), which is what the prototype does.

## Proposed change
**Backend** — add a draft-test endpoint that probes connectivity without persisting:
- `POST /api/v1/connections/test` taking `{ type, env?, config, secret }` → runs the existing `ConnectionAdapter` probe against the ad-hoc config/secret and returns `{ ok }` (same `ConnectionTestResult` shape).
- Reuses the adapter's existing test method; **does not** write a `connections` row or store the secret.
- Security note: a credential travels in the request body (not just the id). Keep it sync-`def`/threadpool like `/test`, never log the secret (PII redactor already covers `secret`), and gate it the same as create.

**Frontend** — add a **Test connection** button to `ConnectionForm` (create mode primarily; edit mode can reuse the saved-connection `/test`). Surface ok/failed inline like the card's health badge.

## Notes
- Surfaced during W6 Phase 4 connection-page prototype-fidelity review.
- Scope is a small backend slice + a button; can ship as its own PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test Connection works on the New/Edit page BEFORE save (draft-connection test endpoint)
- [ ] Draft secrets are not persisted by the test call; clear success/failure surface; tests

# Monitor-kind engine and baseline persistence — map for adding `anomaly`

## 0. Read this first: a skill already exists for this exact task

`/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/.claude/skills/new-monitor-kind/SKILL.md` is a purpose-built traversal guide (registry → run path → authoring → dimension → surfaces → docs → tests) written by this repo's maintainers specifically for adding `anomaly` next. It names exact files/functions and known traps (e.g. #124 dimension round-trip, #937 identifier quoting, #953 unverified feature-matrix ticks). Everything below corroborates/extends it with exact line numbers.

Also notable: `CHECK_KINDS` in `backend/app/db/models.py:81` **already includes `"anomaly"`** (and `"comparison"`), and the `monitor_baselines` migration docstring explicitly says it was built for two consumers — `schema_drift` now and `anomaly` (#593) later, "one persistence shape, no second table later." So **no migration is needed** to add `anomaly`'s DB row-kind or its baseline table — only code.

## 1. Monitor-kind implementation: dispatch, shapes, metric_value/duration_ms/status

**Core engine:** `backend/app/datasources/monitors.py`

- Kind constants: `FRESHNESS = "freshness"` (line 45), `VOLUME = "volume"` (46), `SCHEMA_DRIFT = "schema_drift"` (47).
- **Registry pattern (#726)** — the dispatch mechanism, not an if-chain:
  - `MonitorKindStrategy` dataclass (~line 400): `kind`, `validate_config: Callable[[dict], None]`, `outcome: Callable[[scalar, config, now], CheckOutcome]`, `build_statement: Callable[[TableClause, config], Select] | None`.
  - `MONITOR_KIND_REGISTRY: dict[str, MonitorKindStrategy]` (dict literal, import-time only) — freshness/volume have a `build_statement`; `schema_drift` has `build_statement=None` (routes it to the stateful path instead of the scalar SQL path).
  - Derived tuples (also import-time, never mutated): `MONITOR_KINDS`, `SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS` (kinds with `build_statement is not None`), `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` (kinds with `build_statement is None`).
- **Evaluation-function shape**:
  - `validate_config(kind, config) -> None` — raises `MonitorConfigError` (DB-free structural gate, used both at authoring time and defensively at run time).
  - `build_monitor_statement(kind, *, table, schema, catalog, config) -> Select[Any]` — SQLAlchemy Core statement (never a raw SQL string, per #476 identifier-quoting discipline); raises if the kind has no scalar-SQL form.
  - `monitor_outcome(kind, *, scalar, config, now) -> CheckOutcome` — turns the scalar aggregate result into `CheckOutcome` (`backend/app/datasources/base.py`), which carries `expectation_type`, `success`, `metric_value: float | None`, `observed_value`, `expected_value`, `sample_failures`, `errored`, `error_message`.
- **`monitor_expectation_type(kind) -> str`** — canonical `"monitor:<kind>"` string, single source of truth shared by run path, authoring, and frontend catalog.
- **Per-kind functions** (the freshness/volume "reference shape" a new `anomaly` strategy should mirror):
  - `freshness_column`, `_validate_freshness`, `_freshness_statement`, `_freshness_outcome` — metric = age in hours (`_freshness_age_hours`), higher = worse.
  - `_volume_bounds`, `_validate_volume`, `_volume_statement`, `_volume_outcome` — metric = % deviation outside `[min_rows, max_rows]` (`_volume_deviation_pct`), higher = worse.
  - `_validate_schema_drift`, `_schema_drift_outcome` — metric = drifted-column count (float), scalar is a **dict payload** (not a SQL scalar) computed by the stateful executor.
- **Run-time execution helpers**:
  - `run_monitor_specs(scalar_for, *, monitors, now)` — bands a list of `MonitorSpec`s given a scalar source; isolates a bad monitor to its own `errored` outcome (never fails siblings); routes exceptions through `classify_failure_reason` unless the exception is a `SafeMonitorError` subclass (persisted verbatim — see the `SafeMonitorError`/`MonitorConfigError` docstrings, ~lines 60-115, on what's safe to persist into `results.observed_value`/message given #900/#828/#989).
  - `evaluate_monitors(fetch_scalar, *, table, schema, catalog, monitors)` — SQL-scalar path, builds the statement then calls `fetch_scalar`.
  - `run_monitors_over_engine(engine, *, table, schema, catalog, monitors)` — the shared execution edge SQL runners (Snowflake, Unity Catalog) use: opens one connection, sources every monitor's scalar from it (#428).

**Dispatch by `check.kind` (ADR 0012 seam):** `backend/app/services/run_service.py`, function `_run_outcomes` (lines 115-226):
- `expectation_idx` → GX `CheckRunner.run_checks` (existing GX path).
- `monitor_idx = [... c.kind in SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS]` → runner's `run_monitors` (gated by the runner's advertised `supported_monitor_kinds` capability set, line 198 — **not** `isinstance`, to avoid a Protocol name-match footgun).
- `stateful_idx = [... c.kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS]` → the injected `stateful_monitor_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None` (built by the worker per-run, owns the DB session/baseline store — runners never see it). No executor supplied → per-check `errored` outcome (line 156-165), never a hard failure.
- `comparison_idx` → injected `comparison_executor` (ADR 0015 pattern, same no-executor semantics).
- Any kind not in `{expectation, *MONITOR_KINDS, comparison}` → `NotImplementedError` (line 152) — this is why `anomaly` is currently unreachable at run time even though it's schema-valid.
- `anomaly` (stateful shape, needing a stored baseline like `schema_drift`) would join `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` by registering with `build_statement=None`, and needs its own `build_anomaly_executor`-style injection wired the same way `schema_drift` is (see §2/§7 below, `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:198-210`).

**`metric_value` / `duration_ms` / status production**:
- `metric_value`: For monitors, `CheckOutcome.metric_value` is set directly by the strategy's `outcome()` function (`backend/app/datasources/base.py` ~line 60, doc comment: "the badness scalar a monitor computed directly ... higher = worse"). For GX expectations, `severity.extract_metric` (see §3) pulls `unexpected_percent` from `sample_failures` instead. `severity.extract_metric` prefers `outcome.metric_value` when set (`backend/app/services/severity.py` lines ~30-63).
- `duration_ms`: stays `NULL` in v1 — `backend/app/services/run_service.py:69` comment ("per-check timing isn't separable from GX's single suite-level `validate()`") and ADR 0012 (`docs/adr/0012-monitor-kind-seam.md` line 93, ADR 0016 line 31). Not computed per-monitor at all currently — a new kind gets the same `NULL`.
- Status: produced by `severity.resolve_status`/`derive_status` (see §3) inside `run_service._build_result` (`backend/app/services/run_service.py:64-109`), which maps a `CheckOutcome` + the check's three thresholds to a `Result` row (`status`, `metric_value`, `observed_value`, `expected_value`, `sample_failures`).

## 2. `schema_drift` (#592) baseline persistence shape (PR #876) — the shape #593 (`anomaly`) must reuse

**Model:** `MonitorBaseline` in `backend/app/db/models.py:530-569`, table `monitor_baselines`.

Columns:
- `id` (UUID PK)
- `check_id` — FK `checks.id`, `ondelete="CASCADE"`, not null
- `kind` — `String(32)`, not null, **denormalized** from the check for queryability; check's own `kind` is the authority
- `baseline` — `JSONB`, not null — **kind-shaped payload**; `schema_drift` stores `{"columns": [{"name": ..., "type": ...}, ...]}`. `anomaly` (#593) is explicitly documented (line 536) to reuse this exact shape for its "metric-baseline parameters" JSONB
- `captured_at` — `DateTime(timezone=True)`, server_default `now()`
- `captured_by` — nullable FK `users.id`, `ondelete="SET NULL"`; NULL = run path captured it automatically (first run); non-NULL = manual re-baseline actor
- `created_at`, `updated_at` (standard)

Constraints (`__table_args__`, lines 548-551):
- `UniqueConstraint("check_id", name="uq_monitor_baselines_check")` — **one CURRENT baseline per check**; a re-baseline REPLACES the row (no history kept here — history lives in `results`).
- `_in_check("kind", CHECK_KINDS, "kind_valid")` — CHECK constraint against the shared `CHECK_KINDS` vocabulary (which already admits `"anomaly"`).

**Migration:** `backend/app/alembic/versions/e2f3a4b5c6d7_add_monitor_baselines.py` — creates the table exactly as above, with a **frozen copy** of `CHECK_KINDS` (line 40: `_CHECK_KINDS = ("expectation", "freshness", "volume", "schema_drift", "anomaly", "comparison")` — migrations never import live app code). Its docstring literally states: "Designed for TWO consumers: ... the W5 `anomaly` kind (#593) stores its metric baseline parameters in the same shape, so the payload is a kind-shaped JSONB — one persistence shape, no second table later." **This confirms no new migration is needed for `anomaly`'s baseline storage** — only a differently-shaped JSONB payload under the same table/columns.

**Read/write/re-baseline logic:** `backend/app/services/schema_drift.py`
- `get_baseline(session, check_id) -> MonitorBaseline | None` (select by `check_id`).
- `rebaseline(session, check) -> bool` — **deletes** the row (not an immediate recapture — avoids running introspection on the API request thread); next run recaptures live. Returns whether a row existed.
- `build_schema_drift_executor(session, *, connection, target_table, target_schema, target_catalog, secret_store, persist=True) -> Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome]` — the per-run closure pattern:
  - No baseline row → captures current snapshot, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (constraint="uq_monitor_baselines_check")` (handles concurrent first-runs racing on READ COMMITTED without blowing up the whole run's commit), reports "baseline captured" (`success=True`, `metric_value=0.0`).
  - Baseline row exists → diff current vs stored (`diff_schemas`), band via `monitor_outcome(SCHEMA_DRIFT, scalar=payload, config=config, now=...)`.
  - `persist=False` → dry-run mode: nothing written, missing baseline previews as "would capture."
  - Introspection failure → the **check's** operational error, not the run's (one unreachable target doesn't fail siblings).

**Wiring (worker):** `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:198-210` — builds `stateful_monitor_executor` only when `any(c.kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS for c in checks)`, then passes it into `run_service.execute_run(..., stateful_monitor_executor=...)`. An `anomaly` executor (`build_anomaly_executor`) would be built the same way, gated on `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` membership (which is automatic once registered with `build_statement=None`), and `run_service._run_outcomes` would need it threaded through similarly (it currently only accepts one `stateful_monitor_executor` param serving *all* stateful kinds via `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS`, so both `schema_drift` and `anomaly` executors need to be composed/dispatched — check how `_run_outcomes` calls a single `stateful_monitor_executor(checks[i])` for every stateful-kind index, line 155-167 — the executor closure itself would need to branch on `check.kind` internally, or the signature needs to grow a second executor param, mirroring how `comparison_executor` is a separate param from `stateful_monitor_executor`).

## 3. ADR 0016 severity thresholds → status banding

**Where thresholds live:** columns on `Check` (`backend/app/db/models.py:513-515`): `warn_threshold`, `fail_threshold`, `critical_threshold` — all `Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(Numeric)`. NOT JSONB — plain nullable NUMERIC columns, one check = up to 3 thresholds, kind-agnostic (any kind can set them). Mirrored on `CheckVersion` (lines 611-613) for history snapshots.

**Banding code:** `backend/app/services/severity.py` (ADR 0016, "approach A"):
- `extract_metric(outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Decimal | None` — prefers `outcome.metric_value` (monitor kinds set this directly); else falls back to GX's `unexpected_percent` from `sample_failures`. Uses `Decimal(str(raw))` for exactness; treats non-finite (`NaN`/`inf`) as "no metric."
- `derive_status(*, success, metric_value, warn_threshold, fail_threshold, critical_threshold) -> str` — the pure banding function: `metric_value >= critical_threshold → "critical"`, else `>= fail_threshold → "fail"`, else `>= warn_threshold → "warn"`, else `"pass"`; unset thresholds treated as `+∞`; no thresholds or no metric → binary `pass`/`fail` from `success`.
- `resolve_status(outcome, *, warn_threshold, fail_threshold, critical_threshold) -> tuple[status, metric]` — the single entry point both `run_service._build_result` and `dryrun_service` call, so a dry-run preview can never disagree with what a real run would persist. `outcome.errored=True` short-circuits to `("error", None)` — no tier, no metric.

For `anomaly`, the same thresholds field reuse applies: whatever scalar the anomaly strategy's `outcome()` sets as `CheckOutcome.metric_value` (e.g. a z-score, or a deviation-from-baseline percent — "higher = worse" per the repo's stated convention) gets banded by the *same* generic `derive_status`, no new severity code needed — this is explicitly the ADR 0016 design ("the model generalizes to v1.x freshness/volume monitors ... also 'higher = worse' scalars," `docs/adr/0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md:39`).

## 4. Historical `metric_value` series / results table schema

**`Result` model:** `backend/app/db/models.py:696-726`, table `results`.

Columns: `id`, `run_id` (FK `runs.id`, CASCADE), `check_id` (FK `checks.id`, CASCADE), `status` (`String(16)`, CHECK-constrained to `RESULT_STATUSES`), `metric_value: Decimal | None` (`Numeric`), `duration_ms: Integer | None`, `observed_value`/`expected_value`/`sample_failures` (all `JSONB(none_as_null=True)`), `sample_failures_purged_at`, `created_at`.

Indexes (`__table_args__`, lines 698-701): `Index("ix_results_run_id", "run_id")`, `Index("ix_results_check_id", "check_id")` — no dedicated `metric_value` index; time-series queries join through `Run.created_at`.

**Existing query for a check's historical metric series** (the exact shape an anomaly baseline would build on internally, or query to compute its own rolling stats): `backend/app/services/check_service.py:842-873`, `list_check_result_history(session, suite_id, check_id, *, limit=30) -> list[CheckResultPoint]`:
```
select(Result.run_id, Result.status, Result.metric_value, Run.created_at)
  .join(Run, Result.run_id == Run.id)
  .where(Result.check_id == check_id, Run.suite_id == suite_id)
  .order_by(Run.created_at.desc())
  .limit(limit)
```
rows reversed to chronological order. Surfaced via API at `backend/app/api/v1/checks.py:336` (`list_check_result_history` endpoint). This pattern — join `results` → `runs` on `run_id`, filter `check_id` + `suite_id`, order by `Run.created_at` — is the query shape an `anomaly` monitor's baseline-refresh logic (or its own trend computation) should reuse rather than reinvent.

## 5. `skip` status path (#297/#298)

`RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES = ("skip", "error")` (`backend/app/db/models.py:48`) — orthogonal to the four severity tiers (`pass/warn/fail/critical`), excluded from health-score N, no penalty weight.

`skip` is a **run-level**, not a per-monitor, concept in this codebase: it means "the whole run had nothing to evaluate" (e.g., a flat-file batch hasn't landed yet), not "this one monitor kind decided to skip itself." Persistence: `backend/app/services/run_service.py:332-354`, `skip_run(session, *, run, checks, reason) -> Run` — sets `run.status = "running"` → commits every check a `Result(status="skip", observed_value={"reason": reason})` → `run.status = "succeeded"`. The run still succeeds; only its results are all `skip`.

Called from exactly one place: `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:165` — `run_service.skip_run(session, run=run, checks=checks, reason="batch_not_found")` (flat-file batch resolution failure).

Rendering: `backend/app/services/run_service.py:426-447` computes per-run `(has_error, has_skip)` flags over "operational" statuses for run-list badges; `worst_severity()` (line 65-74) explicitly never ranks `pass`/`skip`/`error`.

For `anomaly`, if a per-check "not enough baseline history yet" case should map to `skip` rather than `pass`/`error`, note that today `skip` is only produced at the whole-run granularity via `skip_run`, never per-check inside `_build_result`/`CheckOutcome`. A per-check anomaly "insufficient history" case would need either (a) a new `errored=False`/special outcome path that `_build_result` maps to `skip` per-check (not currently supported — `_build_result` only derives `error` from `outcome.errored` and the four tiers from `resolve_status`), or (b) treat it as the schema_drift precedent does for "first run" — a passing "baseline captured" result rather than a skip. Tests referencing skip: `backend/tests/integration/test_datasource_runs.py:218`, `backend/tests/services/test_run_service.py:541`, `backend/tests/worker/test_tasks.py:312`, `backend/tests/api/test_runs.py:386-389`.

## 6. Per-kind check config validation

**Structural (DB-free) validation:** `backend/app/datasources/monitors.py`, `validate_monitor_config(kind, config) -> None` (dispatches to `_strategy(kind).validate_config`), each kind's `_validate_<kind>` function:
- `_validate_freshness` (line ~275) → `freshness_column(config)` — validates the optional `column` key as a SQL identifier via `_ident`.
- `_validate_volume` (line ~330) → `_volume_bounds(config)` — validates `min_rows`/`max_rows` as non-negative ints with `min_rows <= max_rows`.
- `_validate_schema_drift` (line ~350) → validates optional `ignore_columns` as a list of identifiers.

An `anomaly` config (window size, sensitivity, target metric) would get its own `_validate_anomaly(config: dict[str, Any]) -> None` here, raising `MonitorConfigError` on bad shape, then registered as the `validate_config` field of its `MonitorKindStrategy` entry.

**Authoring-time gate (with DB/connection-type context):** `backend/app/services/check_service.py`:
- `_V1_SUPPORTED_KINDS = {"expectation", *MONITOR_KINDS, COMPARISON_KIND}` (line 72) — since `MONITOR_KINDS` currently = `{freshness, volume, schema_drift}`, `anomaly` is **not yet authorable** even though it's schema/CHECK-constraint-valid (module docstring lines 10-15 confirms this is deliberate: "`schema_drift`/`anomaly` remain schema-valid but refused"). Adding `anomaly` to `MONITOR_KIND_REGISTRY` in `monitors.py` automatically widens `_V1_SUPPORTED_KINDS` (it derives from `MONITOR_KINDS`).
- `validate_kind(kind)` (line 136) — the general "kind is in `_V1_SUPPORTED_KINDS`" 422 gate.
- `validate_monitor_check(kind, config, *, expectation_type, connection_type, fail_threshold, critical_threshold)` (lines 195-262) — the freshness/volume/schema_drift-shaped authoring validator: (1) datasource-capability gate via `MONITOR_CAPABLE_TYPES` (scalar) or `SCHEMA_DRIFT_CAPABLE_TYPES` (stateful, line 224-234 — selects the capability set by `kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS`, so `anomaly` as a stateful kind would need its own `ANOMALY_CAPABLE_TYPES` frozenset here or reuse `SCHEMA_DRIFT_CAPABLE_TYPES`); (2) `expectation_type` must equal `monitor_expectation_type(kind)`; (3) config-shape via `validate_monitor_config`; (4) kind-specific extra gates (freshness's column/threshold requirements at lines 251-262 — an `anomaly` kind would likely need an analogous "needs at least N historical points" or "needs a target metric configured" gate here).
- `MONITOR_CAPABLE_TYPES` (line 92), `SCHEMA_DRIFT_CAPABLE_TYPES` (line 98) — per-datasource capability frozensets that `anomaly` will need its own variant of (or reuse) depending on what data it needs (likely just needs the check's own historical `results.metric_value` series, not the live datasource, so its capability set might be "any connection type that already has other checks producing metrics" rather than SQL/file-specific).

**Export/import validation:** `backend/app/services/suite_io_service.py` — imports `MONITOR_KINDS` (line 32), branches `if c["kind"] in MONITOR_KINDS:` (line 183) to call the monitor validator, `elif c["kind"] == COMPARISON_KIND:` (line 192) for comparison. Validation is atomic (every check validated before any row written, per module docstring line 14). `anomaly` joining `MONITOR_KINDS` automatically routes it into the existing monitor-validation branch here.

`backend/app/services/dryrun_service.py`:
- `dry_run_check(connection, *, kind, expectation_type, config, warn_threshold, fail_threshold, critical_threshold, target, secret_store) -> DryRunOutcome` (lines 71-...): explicitly branches `if kind == SCHEMA_DRIFT: return _dry_run_schema_drift(...)` (line 97-100); `if kind != _EXPECTATION_KIND: raise DryRunUnsupportedError(...)` (line 101-105) — so **any kind other than `expectation`/`schema_drift` is currently a 422** at dry-run time. ## 1. Monitor-kind implementation: dispatch, shapes, metric_value/duration_ms/status

**Core engine:** `backend/app/datasources/monitors.py`

- Kind constants: `FRESHNESS = "freshness"` (line 45), `VOLUME = "volume"` (46), `SCHEMA_DRIFT = "schema_drift"` (47).
- **Registry pattern (#726)** — the dispatch mechanism, not an if-chain:
  - `MonitorKindStrategy` dataclass (~line 400): `kind`, `validate_config: Callable[[dict], None]`, `outcome: Callable[[scalar, config, now], CheckOutcome]`, `build_statement: Callable[[TableClause, config], Select] | None`.
  - `MONITOR_KIND_REGISTRY: dict[str, MonitorKindStrategy]` (dict literal, import-time only) — freshness/volume have a `build_statement`; `schema_drift` has `build_statement=None` (routes it to the stateful path instead of the scalar SQL path).
  - Derived tuples (also import-time, never mutated): `MONITOR_KINDS`, `SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS` (kinds with `build_statement is not None`), `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` (kinds with `build_statement is None`).
- **Evaluation-function shape**:
  - `validate_config(kind, config) -> None` — raises `MonitorConfigError` (DB-free structural gate, used both at authoring time and defensively at run time).
  - `build_monitor_statement(kind, *, table, schema, catalog, config) -> Select[Any]` — SQLAlchemy Core statement (never a raw SQL string, per #476 identifier-quoting discipline); raises if the kind has no scalar-SQL form.
  - `monitor_outcome(kind, *, scalar, config, now) -> CheckOutcome` — turns the scalar aggregate result into `CheckOutcome` (`backend/app/datasources/base.py`), which carries `expectation_type`, `success`, `metric_value: float | None`, `observed_value`, `expected_value`, `sample_failures`, `errored`, `error_message`.
- **`monitor_expectation_type(kind) -> str`** — canonical `"monitor:<kind>"` string, single source of truth shared by run path, authoring, and frontend catalog.
- **Per-kind functions** (the freshness/volume "reference shape" a new `anomaly` strategy should mirror):
  - `freshness_column`, `_validate_freshness`, `_freshness_statement`, `_freshness_outcome` — metric = age in hours (`_freshness_age_hours`), higher = worse.
  - `_volume_bounds`, `_validate_volume`, `_volume_statement`, `_volume_outcome` — metric = % deviation outside `[min_rows, max_rows]` (`_volume_deviation_pct`), higher = worse.
  - `_validate_schema_drift`, `_schema_drift_outcome` — metric = drifted-column count (float), scalar is a **dict payload** (not a SQL scalar) computed by the stateful executor.
- **Run-time execution helpers**:
  - `run_monitor_specs(scalar_for, *, monitors, now)` — bands a list of `MonitorSpec`s given a scalar source; isolates a bad monitor to its own `errored` outcome (never fails siblings); routes exceptions through `classify_failure_reason` unless the exception is a `SafeMonitorError` subclass (persisted verbatim — see the `SafeMonitorError`/`MonitorConfigError` docstrings, ~lines 60-115, on what's safe to persist into `results.observed_value`/message given #900/#828/#989).
  - `evaluate_monitors(fetch_scalar, *, table, schema, catalog, monitors)` — SQL-scalar path, builds the statement then calls `fetch_scalar`.
  - `run_monitors_over_engine(engine, *, table, schema, catalog, monitors)` — the shared execution edge SQL runners (Snowflake, Unity Catalog) use: opens one connection, sources every monitor's scalar from it (#428).

**Dispatch by `check.kind` (ADR 0012 seam):** `backend/app/services/run_service.py`, function `_run_outcomes` (lines 115-226):
- `expectation_idx` → GX `CheckRunner.run_checks` (existing GX path).
- `monitor_idx = [... c.kind in SCALAR_MONITOR_KINDS]` → runner's `run_monitors` (gated by the runner's advertised `supported_monitor_kinds` capability set, line 198 — **not** `isinstance`, to avoid a Protocol name-match footgun).
- `stateful_idx = [... c.kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS]` → the injected `stateful_monitor_executor: Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome] | None` (built by the worker per-run, owns the DB session/baseline store — runners never see it). No executor supplied → per-check `errored` outcome (line 156-165), never a hard failure.
- `comparison_idx` → injected `comparison_executor` (ADR 0015 pattern, same no-executor semantics).
- Any kind not in `{expectation, *MONITOR_KINDS, comparison}` → `NotImplementedError` (line 152) — this is why `anomaly` is currently unreachable at run time even though it's schema-valid.
- `anomaly` (stateful shape, needing a stored baseline like `schema_drift`) would join `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` by registering with `build_statement=None`, and needs its own `build_anomaly_executor`-style injection wired the same way `schema_drift` is (see §2/§7 below, `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:198-210`).

**`metric_value` / `duration_ms` / status production**:
- `metric_value`: For monitors, `CheckOutcome.metric_value` is set directly by the strategy's `outcome()` function (`backend/app/datasources/base.py` ~line 60, doc comment: "the badness scalar a monitor computed directly ... higher = worse"). For GX expectations, `severity.extract_metric` (see §3) pulls `unexpected_percent` from `sample_failures` instead. `severity.extract_metric` prefers `outcome.metric_value` when set (`backend/app/services/severity.py` lines ~30-63).
- `duration_ms`: stays `NULL` in v1 — `backend/app/services/run_service.py:69` comment ("per-check timing isn't separable from GX's single suite-level `validate()`") and ADR 0012 (`docs/adr/0012-monitor-kind-seam.md` line 93, ADR 0016 line 31). Not computed per-monitor at all currently — a new kind gets the same `NULL`.
- Status: produced by `severity.resolve_status`/`derive_status` (see §3) inside `run_service._build_result` (`backend/app/services/run_service.py:64-109`), which maps a `CheckOutcome` + the check's three thresholds to a `Result` row (`status`, `metric_value`, `observed_value`, `expected_value`, `sample_failures`).

## 2. `schema_drift` (#592) baseline persistence shape (PR #876) — the shape #593 (`anomaly`) must reuse

**Model:** `MonitorBaseline` in `backend/app/db/models.py:530-569`, table `monitor_baselines`.

Columns:
- `id` (UUID PK)
- `check_id` — FK `checks.id`, `ondelete="CASCADE"`, not null
- `kind` — `String(32)`, not null, **denormalized** from the check for queryability; check's own `kind` is the authority
- `baseline` — `JSONB`, not null — **kind-shaped payload**; `schema_drift` stores `{"columns": [{"name": ..., "type": ...}, ...]}`. `anomaly` (#593) is explicitly documented (line 536) to reuse this exact shape for its "metric-baseline parameters" JSONB
- `captured_at` — `DateTime(timezone=True)`, server_default `now()`
- `captured_by` — nullable FK `users.id`, `ondelete="SET NULL"`; NULL = run path captured it automatically (first run); non-NULL = manual re-baseline actor
- `created_at`, `updated_at` (standard)

Constraints (`__table_args__`, lines 548-551):
- `UniqueConstraint("check_id", name="uq_monitor_baselines_check")` — **one CURRENT baseline per check**; a re-baseline REPLACES the row (no history kept here — history lives in `results`).
- `_in_check("kind", CHECK_KINDS, "kind_valid")` — CHECK constraint against the shared `CHECK_KINDS` vocabulary (which already admits `"anomaly"`).

**Migration:** `backend/app/alembic/versions/e2f3a4b5c6d7_add_monitor_baselines.py` — creates the table exactly as above, with a **frozen copy** of `CHECK_KINDS` (line 40: `_CHECK_KINDS = ("expectation", "freshness", "volume", "schema_drift", "anomaly", "comparison")` — migrations never import live app code). Its docstring literally states: "Designed for TWO consumers: ... the W5 `anomaly` kind (#593) stores its metric baseline parameters in the same shape, so the payload is a kind-shaped JSONB — one persistence shape, no second table later." **This confirms no new migration is needed for `anomaly`'s baseline storage** — only a differently-shaped JSONB payload under the same table/columns.

**Read/write/re-baseline logic:** `backend/app/services/schema_drift.py`
- `get_baseline(session, check_id) -> MonitorBaseline | None` (select by `check_id`).
- `rebaseline(session, check) -> bool` — **deletes** the row (not an immediate recapture — avoids running introspection on the API request thread); next run recaptures live. Returns whether a row existed.
- `build_schema_drift_executor(session, *, connection, target_table, target_schema, target_catalog, secret_store, persist=True) -> Callable[[Check], CheckOutcome]` — the per-run closure pattern:
  - No baseline row → captures current snapshot, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (constraint="uq_monitor_baselines_check")` (handles concurrent first-runs racing on READ COMMITTED without blowing up the whole run's commit), reports "baseline captured" (`success=True`, `metric_value=0.0`).
  - Baseline row exists → diff current vs stored (`diff_schemas`), band via `monitor_outcome(SCHEMA_DRIFT, scalar=payload, config=config, now=...)`.
  - `persist=False` → dry-run mode: nothing written, missing baseline previews as "would capture."
  - Introspection failure → the **check's** operational error, not the run's (one unreachable target doesn't fail siblings).

**Wiring (worker):** `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:198-210` — builds `stateful_monitor_executor` only when `any(c.kind in STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS for c in checks)`, then passes it into `run_service.execute_run(..., stateful_monitor_executor=...)`. An `anomaly` executor (`build_anomaly_executor`) would be built the same way, gated on `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS` membership (which is automatic once registered with `build_statement=None`), and `run_service._run_outcomes` would need it threaded through similarly (it currently only accepts one `stateful_monitor_executor` param serving *all* stateful kinds via `STATEFUL_MONITOR_KINDS`, so both `schema_drift` and `anomaly` executors need to be composed/dispatched — check how `_run_outcomes` calls a single `stateful_monitor_executor(checks[i])` for every stateful-kind index, line 155-167 — the executor closure itself would need to branch on `check.kind` internally, or the signature needs to grow a second executor param, mirroring how `comparison_executor` is a separate param from `stateful_monitor_executor`).

## 3. ADR 0016 severity thresholds → status banding

**Where thresholds live:** columns on `Check` (`backend/app/db/models.py:513-515`): `warn_threshold`, `fail_threshold`, `critical_threshold` — all `Mapped[Decimal | None] = mapped_column(Numeric)`. NOT JSONB — plain nullable NUMERIC columns, one check = up to 3 thresholds, kind-agnostic (any kind can set them). Mirrored on `CheckVersion` (lines 611-613) for history snapshots.

**Banding code:** `backend/app/services/severity.py` (ADR 0016, "approach A"):
- `extract_metric(outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Decimal | None` — prefers `outcome.metric_value` (monitor kinds set this directly); else falls back to GX's `unexpected_percent` from `sample_failures`. Uses `Decimal(str(raw))` for exactness; treats non-finite (`NaN`/`inf`) as "no metric."
- `derive_status(*, success, metric_value, warn_threshold, fail_threshold, critical_threshold) -> str` — the pure banding function: `metric_value >= critical_threshold → "critical"`, else `>= fail_threshold → "fail"`, else `>= warn_threshold → "warn"`, else `"pass"`; unset thresholds treated as `+∞`; no thresholds or no metric → binary `pass`/`fail` from `success`.
- `resolve_status(outcome, *, warn_threshold, fail_threshold, critical_threshold) -> tuple[status, metric]` — the single entry point both `run_service._build_result` and `dryrun_service` call, so a dry-run preview can never disagree with what a real run would persist. `outcome.errored=True` short-circuits to `("error", None)` — no tier, no metric.

For `anomaly`, the same thresholds field reuse applies: whatever scalar the anomaly strategy's `outcome()` sets as `CheckOutcome.metric_value` (e.g. a z-score, or a deviation-from-baseline percent — "higher = worse" per the repo's stated convention) gets banded by the *same* generic `derive_status`, no new severity code needed — this is explicitly the ADR 0016 design ("the model generalizes to v1.x freshness/volume monitors ... also 'higher = worse' scalars," `docs/adr/0016-severity-derivation-semantics.md:39`).

## 4. Historical `metric_value` series / results table schema

**`Result` model:** `backend/app/db/models.py:696-726`, table `results`.

Columns: `id`, `run_id` (FK `runs.id`, CASCADE), `check_id` (FK `checks.id`, CASCADE), `status` (`String(16)`, CHECK-constrained to `RESULT_STATUSES`), `metric_value: Decimal | None` (`Numeric`), `duration_ms: Integer | None`, `observed_value`/`expected_value`/`sample_failures` (all `JSONB(none_as_null=True)`), `sample_failures_purged_at`, `created_at`.

Indexes (`__table_args__`, lines 698-701): `Index("ix_results_run_id", "run_id")`, `Index("ix_results_check_id", "check_id")` — no dedicated `metric_value` index; time-series queries join through `Run.created_at`.

**Existing query for a check's historical metric series** (the exact shape an anomaly baseline would build on internally, or query to compute its own rolling stats): `backend/app/services/check_service.py:842-873`, `list_check_result_history(session, suite_id, check_id, *, limit=30) -> list[CheckResultPoint]`:
```
select(Result.run_id, Result.status, Result.metric_value, Run.created_at)
  .join(Run, Result.run_id == Run.id)
  .where(Result.check_id == check_id, Run.suite_id == suite_id)
  .order_by(Run.created_at.desc())
  .limit(limit)
```
rows reversed to chronological order. Surfaced via API at `backend/app/api/v1/checks.py:336` (`list_check_result_history` endpoint). This pattern — join `results` → `runs` on `run_id`, filter `check_id` + `suite_id`, order by `Run.created_at` — is the query shape an `anomaly` monitor's baseline-refresh logic (or its own trend computation) should reuse rather than reinvent.

## 5. `skip` status path (#297/#298)

`RESULT_OPERATIONAL_STATUSES = ("skip", "error")` (`backend/app/db/models.py:48`) — orthogonal to the four severity tiers (`pass/warn/fail/critical`), excluded from health-score N, no penalty weight.

`skip` is a **run-level**, not a per-monitor, concept in this codebase: it means "the whole run had nothing to evaluate" (e.g., a flat-file batch hasn't landed yet), not "this one monitor kind decided to skip itself." Persistence: `backend/app/services/run_service.py:332-354`, `skip_run(session, *, run, checks, reason) -> Run` — sets `run.status = "running"` → commits every check a `Result(status="skip", observed_value={"reason": reason})` → `run.status = "succeeded"`. The run still succeeds; only its results are all `skip`.

Called from exactly one place: `backend/app/worker/tasks.py:165` — `run_service.skip_run(session, run=run, checks=checks, reason="batch_not_found")` (flat-file batch resolution failure).

Rendering: `backend/app/services/run_service.py:426-447` computes per-run `(has_error, has_skip)` flags over "operational" statuses for run-list badges; `worst_severity()` (line 65-74) explicitly never ranks `pass`/`skip`/`error`.

For `anomaly`, if a per-check "not enough baseline history yet" case should map to `skip` rather than `pass`/`error`, note that today `skip` is only produced at the whole-run granularity via `skip_run`, never per-check inside `_build_result`/`CheckOutcome`. A per-check anomaly "insufficient history" case would need either (a) a new `errored=False`/special outcome path that `_build_result` maps to `skip` per-check (not currently supported — `_build_result` only derives `error` from `outcome.errored` and the four tiers from `resolve_status`), or (b) treat it as the schema_drift precedent does for "first run" — a passing "baseline captured" result rather than a skip. Tests referencing skip: `backend/tests/integration/test_datasource_runs.py:218`, `backend/tests/services/test_run_service.py:541`, `backend/tests/worker/test_tasks.py:312`, `backend/tests/api/test_runs.py:386-389`.
