Shipped as part 1 of 2 deliberately: a `workflow_dispatch` workflow must be on the default branch before it can be dispatched, and pointing `ci.yml` at packages that do not exist yet would red the gate it protects. **#278:** the 63 mutmut survivors in `custom_sql.py` — the lexical guard on an injection surface — triaged to **142 killed / 29 survived / 14 timeout** (from 113/63/9; detection 65.9% → 83.2%). **The review found a real multi-statement bypass, via arithmetic:** an agent noticed the triage comment's category counts summed to 29 against 31 survivors and called the completeness claim unverifiable; re-counting exactly showed two omitted categories, one of which was `_strip_noncode`'s closing-quote branch skipping the next character — so `SELECT 'a'; SELECT 1` strips to `SELECT   SELECT 1` and passes the multi-statement guard, with no forbidden keyword to catch it and the existing escaped-quote test covering the opposite case. **Lesson, twice over: an estimate inside a completeness claim is where a defect hides, and reasoning about mutant equivalence is unreliable in both directions** — comparing the scanner's raw output first said all 7 quote mutants were real gaps (4 are unkillable, proven by ~37,600 fuzz strings plus a derivation); measuring at the observable boundary, `validate_query`'s verdict, was the only thing that settled it. Two comment overclaims were also found independently by two agents and fixed.) (**2026-07-25 (later still) — Batch 3 CLOSED: #898 done both halves.** Backend (#1011): five warehouse-lineage gaps, each verified by re-applying its own mutant. The one that matters is `_from_object_dependencies`'s `continue`→`break` — the spike killed nothing because every fixture exercising the domain filter had its non-table row at the **end**, where `continue` and `break` are indistinguishable; with a FUNCTION-domain row in the **middle** the mutant silently drops every remaining edge, the #845-class omission of asserting 'nothing feeds this view' when we merely stopped looking. Two items were **dispositioned rather than fixed**: `_account_has_write_activity` no longer exists (code moved since the July spike), and the GET_LINEAGE success shape is **unreachable in production** — `_from_get_lineage` probes then always raises, the per-seed traversal being a deferred #858 slice, so those mutants survive for want of a reachable path, not an assertion. Frontend (#1012): Stryker 81.84% → **90.14%**, survivors 57 → 30; `lineageLayout` 66.3 → **88.6** because its **geometry — the module's whole output — was unasserted**: the existing tests pin RELATIVE facts ('depth-2 sits beyond depth-1') that survive almost any arithmetic mutation, so column centring, row spacing and the bezier control points mutated freely. Pinned as invariants, not hardcoded constants. `health.ts`'s ladder is now table-driven per rung **with colour asserted alongside every label** (#563's class), and `assetTree`'s comparators — which mutated to `true`/`false`/`() => undefined` with the suite green — now have ORDER asserted, not just membership. **Two of my own test bugs were caught only by running them** (`NODE_H` never imported; an SVG-path destructure assuming a leading token, so a control-offset assertion read `sy` as `sx` and 'passed' against 0) — the same lesson as the #278 arithmetic: a test you have not watched fail proves nothing.) (**2026-07-25 (later still) — Batch 4 opened: #842 + #843 shipped together.** They had to be one PR: #843's 'set only on a successful publish' has to live INSIDE the task #842 introduces, so splitting them would have built the same state machine twice. **#842:** the health publish ran synchronously inside the connection loop inside the beat task — Teams (10s) + Slack (10s) + SMTP (15s) per crossing — and the failure mode that matters is the CORRELATED one: a DataQ-side outage makes every orchestration connection cross on the same sweep, so ten of them bolted ~6 minutes of blocking sends onto a task that beats every 10 minutes. **#843:** both edges now ride a new `connections.health_alerted_at` written after a successful publish, not the failure counter — delivery is best-effort, so an operator could be told an alarm had ENDED that they were never told had BEGUN. That also removed the `==` the old docstring apologised for (a connection past a newly-lowered threshold never lands on the equality again, so it never alerted at all). **The review earned its keep twice.** It caught that `>=` gave up a safety property `==` had BY CONSTRUCTION — only one of two serialized streak values can equal the threshold, so overlapping sweeps could not both alert; with `>=` they can, so the task now CLAIMS the edge with one atomic conditional UPDATE and releases the claim if the send fails. It also found a test that was not load-bearing (streaks 4/5/144/1008, none equal to the default threshold of 3, so a revert to `==` would have stayed green). One finding was **verified-benign and recorded rather than changed**: a failed RECOVERED publish leaves the flag set and suppresses a later FAILING alert — deliberate, since the operator's last delivered state is already 'failing', and it self-heals on the next healthy sweep. **Also learned: the three 'unexplained' test errors I nearly shipped a WIP PR over were my own un-migrated local dev DB** — those lock tests use `SessionLocal()` (the APP database, not the test schema, because a real `FOR UPDATE` needs a second committed connection), and I had been running ALTER against the wrong database. The migration checklist item — up/down/up locally — was the thing I had skipped.) (**2026-07-25 (later still) — Batch 4 CLOSED with #784.** The rate-limit socket timeouts bound the penalty when Redis is DOWN; they do nothing when it is UP AND DEGRADED, and this is the innermost middleware over /api + /mcp + webhooks, so every request serially waits out the full timeout and the app's p99 becomes Redis's p99 while we keep hammering a struggling server. A breaker now opens after 5 CONSECUTIVE failures for 5s and returns the fail-open signal without awaiting; reopening is a single probe with no extra state. Consecutive, not a rate — a Redis dropping one request in five is annoying, not degraded, and opening for it would silently switch enforcement off across the whole API. **The review found two things worth the ink.** (1) A straggling success could close an open breaker: every request is an independent asyncio task over shared module globals, so one that passed the gate just BEFORE the trip and resolved just after would retroactively close a breaker others had legitimately opened — and a degraded Redis serves exactly that mix of slow successes and timeouts, so it would flap under precisely the traffic it exists to handle. (2) **I reintroduced this PR's own lesson two tests later:** the probe test asserted only that the call returned None while open, which fail-open does anyway, so it passed with the breaker removed entirely — the same vacuity the timed test in the same PR was written to avoid. **Standing lesson, now three-for-three this session: assert the thing that CHANGES, not the thing that is true either way.** Fail-open already returned None; what #784 changes is that the calls STOP, so the fake counts its calls.) (**2026-07-25 (later still) — Batch 5 opened with #976.** `import * as monaco from 'monaco-editor'` resolves to `esm/vs/index.js`, which registers EVERY language Monaco ships, so Vite emitted a worker chunk per language service: **five workers, 9.46 MB, four of which `getWorker` never returned**. The component's own docstring already said only the base worker was needed — the import contradicted it. Now imports `editor/editor.api.js` and registers SQL alone (lazily, so the grammar is a small async chunk and no language SERVICE tags along). Measured: workers 5/9.46 MB → 1/300 kB, monaco js 4,385 → 2,648 kB, css 162 → 79 kB. **Verified as the right thing, not just a smaller number** — a broken editor would also shrink the bundle, so the check was that the build now registers exactly one language (`id:`sql``) where it previously carried the full set. Also found a **dead mock that predated the change**: the test named a pre-0.56 `esm/vs/...worker` path the component had stopped importing, so the real worker module was loading underneath a test that implied isolation it did not have. A mock whose specifier does not match is worse than no mock. Remaining in Batch 5: #936 (3-part catalog/schema quoting — needs a dialect passed into `core_table`, since hand-rolling the quote char is the exact dialect mistake that function exists to avoid), #788 (surface `retry_after_seconds` on 429), #925 (assets paging past the 200-row cap).) (**2026-07-26 — PROD REDEPLOYED to `c401572d`.** Prod had sat on `dff6d958` while a month of merged work accumulated, so this deploy carried Batches 1–5 in one roll: #954/#838 connection health + credential expiry, #882/#942/#943 bounded flat-file reads, #990/#993/#787/#278/#898 gate integrity, #842/#843 alerting, #784 the rate-limit breaker, and #976 the Monaco trim. Three migrations applied (a CHECK-constraint rename plus two nullable column adds — all additive, all tested up/down/up locally); the migrate job ran to Succeeded BEFORE the apps rolled, which is why a column-adding migration can ship with its code here. Post-deploy smoke green: `/healthz` 200, api 401 (auth enforced), SPA + deep-link 200, beat started clean with the watchdog armed and no NoneType crash. **#976 was verified against PROD, not just the local build** — the deployed `monaco-*.js` carries the same content hash as the local artifact, registers exactly one language (`id:`sql``), and the four unused worker chunks now 404 while `editor.worker` serves 200. That is the check the PR flagged as outstanding, now discharged: chunk size alone would have looked identical if the editor were simply broken.) (**2026-07-26 (later) — #788 PARTIAL: two ACs shipped, one pulled after implementing it.** The backend had always sent `Retry-After` + `detail.retry_after_seconds` (ADR 0035) and **nothing read either** — a grep across `frontend/src` returned zero hits — so a throttled user saw 'Too many requests' and no idea whether to retry now or in a minute. Now folded into `error.message` at the interceptor, so every call site gains it without learning about rate limiting; fractional waits round UP (rounding down advises a retry while still throttled, producing a second 429), and an HTTP-date `Retry-After` yields undefined rather than NaN. **AC 3 was written, then reverted:** holding the last-known `is_workspace_admin` through a throttled `/me` turned out to be an unreachable path — after a successful load `MeProvider` only refetches via the retry timer a 429 itself sets, so a cached `ok` is never the state a later 429 lands on. It would have shipped with a comment describing behaviour the code did not have. The case that actually happens is the FIRST `/me` being throttled, where there is no cached answer to hold and the fix is to stay loading and retry — a different shape from the issue's sketch. **Writing the test is what exposed it**, which is the session's recurring lesson arriving from the other direction: not a test that proves nothing, but a test that refuses to be written because the behaviour isn't there.) (**2026-07-26 (later) — LIVE TESTING against the fresh prod deploy found a real defect that three green suites could not.** A non-interactive bearer (`az account get-access-token` on the api scope, #565) against `/api/v1/connections` showed **both Airflow connections at 282 and 280 consecutive poll failures** — ~47 hours broken. **That diagnosis was WRONG and is corrected on the issue** — I read the 404 and the `/api/v1/` URL shape and concluded Airflow 3 had moved the API to `/api/v2/`, without checking whether the host was up. It is not: `dataq-harness-airflow` is **`Stopped`**, deliberately, per the 2026-07-04 cost wind-down (#590), and ACA's ingress serves its unavailable page with a 404. `/api/v2/version` returns the same Azure error page, which would have said so immediately. [#1023](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1023) is rescoped to what survives: the classified reason tells the operator to check a connection config that is fine, when the signal is really that the host is unreachable — and a deliberately-offline integration now accumulates unbounded failures AND alerts (#842/#843), which wants a decision rather than a default. **The lesson is the one already written down and not applied: verify the reason, not just the result** — a green-looking inference from a status code is still an inference. Two things worth keeping: **#828's health counter is what made it findable at all** — that fact used to live only in logs — and **the classified reason points the wrong way**, telling the operator to 'check the connection and the suite's run target' when nothing is wrong with either; a 404 from a KNOWN provider endpoint is a version-compatibility signal, not a user misconfiguration. Also filed [#1024](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1024): `credential_expires_at` is NULL on all 13 prod connections including the two SAS-bearing ADLS ones, because #838 computes on secret write plus a DAILY sweep — so on a fresh deploy the feature delivers nothing for the existing estate for up to 24h, and NULL now means both 'no readable expiry' and 'not looked yet', which the UI cannot distinguish. **Neither would have surfaced from any test: one needed a live provider at its real version, the other needed a deploy with pre-existing rows.**) (**2026-07-26 (later still) — #788 CLOSED**, the last AC landing in the shape that actually occurs rather than the one sketched. The per-IP unauth bucket is shared across endpoints, so a burst anywhere can 429 `/me` — and painting PageError for it is wrong twice over: the app is fine, and the answer arrives on its own seconds later, meanwhile a workspace admin has lost the Admin and Settings nav. `MeProvider` now stays in `loading` and retries when the server said to; a spinner is the honest state where an error page asserts something false. Bounded at three retries, because **an endless spinner is the one outcome worse than an error page** — indistinguishable from a hung app, with nothing to act on. Non-429 failures are untouched (a 500/403 is not self-healing and must reach PageError with its HTTP facts, #910/#930). The mutation check earned its keep twice: it confirmed all three retry tests are load-bearing, AND it exposed a leak in those tests — `vi.useRealTimers()` sat at the end of each test BODY, which a failing test never reaches, so fake timers bled into the next test and it timed out for a reason unrelated to its assertion. Three real failures plus one phantom; moved to `afterEach`. **Batch 5 now stands at #976 and #788 done, #936 and #925 open.**) (**2026-07-26 (end of day) — ops log + hook, and HARNESS_TODO retired.** Two incidents this week shared one shape: state that mattered lived only outside git, so nobody could tell a deliberate action from a fault. New [docs/ops-log.md](ops-log.md) records harness start/stop and credential rotation — the latter listing EVERY Key Vault secret written per rotation, the countermeasure to the partial rotation that left two Snowflake connections dead for three weeks. Git-tracked deliberately rather than harness-side: history is the point, and an untracked file has none. A `PostToolUse:Bash` hook keeps it current; **it took three attempts and every failure was the same mistake** — it fired on its own commit message (grepped the whole string), then still fired after anchoring (prose WORD-WRAPS, so a line began `harness_window.sh.`), and finally needed a whitespace-or-end boundary, because a real invocation is followed by arguments or nothing, never a full stop. Then I chased a fourth phantom before testing the real hook against the real command and finding it silent. **Three variations of reasoning about what a pattern would match instead of running it** — the same root as the Airflow misdiagnosis that morning. **`HARNESS_TODO.md` removed**, but only after reading it: it held TWO open items, not the one already filed. The second — the deployed Terraform still injects `SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD` into the Airflow ACA env and dbt job, dead under the 2026-07-18 MFA enforcement — **would have been destroyed with the file**, and is invisible today only because the harness is stopped. Now [#1030](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1030) and [#1032](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1032), original archived verbatim in #1032. It also supplied the *why* Azure never could: the harness was stopped ~15 min after that MFA wall. **Rule now recorded: anything still open belongs in the tracker; only settled notes belong harness-side.**) (**2026-07-26 (close) — #1024 cold-start half fixed.** `refresh_credential_expiry` ran DAILY, which is right for a value that only moves on a rotation and wrong for a cold start: a freshly deployed instance showed `credential_expires_at` NULL until the first tick, and **NULL renders as 'nothing expires soon' — indistinguishable from 'we have not looked yet'**, so the warning surface read as reassuring for up to 24h. Prod had exactly that after this morning's deploy, including the SAS-bearing connections whose expiry is printed in the token. Now dispatched from `beat_init` beside the existing gap recovery (one beat process per deployment → once per restart, not once per worker). The two startup tasks became a list with **independently guarded** dispatch — a single `try` around the loop would let the first broker hiccup silently drop every later task, and that failure looks identical to success because dispatch is fire-and-forget. Mutation-verified both ways. **#1024 stays OPEN for its second half**: NULL still conflates 'no readable expiry' (a Snowflake PAT — correctly unknowable) with 'not computed yet'; this shrinks the ambiguity window from a day to seconds without removing it.) (**2026-07-26 — TIER 1 (security) DONE: #989 closed.** A monitor's error message interpolated the offending target CELL, and that message is safe-marked — persisted verbatim into `results.observed_value` and rendered in the UI, alerts and MCP, none of which consult the suite's column policy. A freshness monitor aimed at a declared-PII column echoed its value straight past the redaction machinery built for exactly that. It also made the marker's own rule false, which is how a rule erodes. **Built at the READ layer, not by threading a policy into `datasources/`** — my first scoping said the latter; reading `redact_sample_failures` showed the product already stores samples raw and masks at the read boundaries, so threading a policy down would have inverted that dependency to fix a redaction bug. Message is now value-free by construction; the cell rides `MonitorConfigError.unparsed_value` and is masked by the new `redact_observed_value` under the same authority as the sample path (shown unless *known* sensitive — default-masking would make 'your timestamp column has junk in it' unactionable, the reason option (a) was rejected). **The review earned its keep: it found a FOURTH sink I had missed** — `/_probe/runs/{run_id}` mapped Result rows straight through Pydantic, so a cell masked everywhere else surfaced raw there. Fixed with a test. That is the failure mode of per-sink redaction, and why each sink needs its own test rather than one test for 'the redactor'. It also surfaced something worse, filed as [#1039](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1039): that route has **no suite-ownership check at all**, so any authenticated user with a run UUID reads any run's results, bypassing ADR 0027 — and it is mounted in prod. Two bugs on one forgotten Week-1 route in a single PR is an argument for deleting it.) (**2026-07-26 — TIER 2 (connection health) DONE: #998, #1024, #748, #999, #996.** Sequenced by dependency, and the order mattered every time. **#998** replaced the connection-wide failure count with per-suite streaks rolled up — a broken hourly suite used to fill the shared 20-run window and badge a connection whose credential was fine, telling the operator to re-auth something that worked; a connection is now degraded only when EVERY suite is failing, with the MINIMUM streak as the number (the strongest claim true of all of them). **#1024** gave NULL expiry one meaning via `credential_expiry_checked_at` — stamped on every read, so 'no readable expiry' stops being indistinguishable from 'never looked', which is what made an unchecked credential look safe. **#748** added `/readyz` (a real DB read, 2s-bounded) because during the 2026-07-10 lock incident `/healthz` stayed GREEN through 25 minutes of total read degradation; `/healthz` stays liveness-only on purpose, since a liveness probe that fails on a DB blip gets the container killed. **#999** is the one where measuring changed the answer: the planned index ALONE only halves a cost that stays linear in history (8.4→32.7→195.4ms at 1k/4k/16k runs per suite; with index 5.5→23.0→94.8ms). LATERAL alone is also linear. Only **both** are flat — **0.2ms at every size** — because the index lets Postgres stop after 20 entries per suite. AC 3 said 'measured, not assumed' and it was right to. **#996** then fired the alert edges off the run streak, reusing #843's delivery-driven logic rather than a second copy. **Three guards caught things I would have shipped:** two alembic revision-id COLLISIONS (I verified the id for one migration then hand-picked the next), the #990 model-vs-migration parity test catching the new index undeclared, and the #787 assert-side-effect guard catching my own test. **And a mutation survived that mattered** — deleting #996's hook from `run_suite` broke nothing, so the alerting could have shipped connected to nothing. Third instance this session of a safeguard that looks wired up and isn't, after the dead mock in #976 and the unwired redaction sink in #989.) (**2026-07-26 (night) — TIER 3 under way: #1039, #727, #905.** **#1039** deleted the unauthorized probe run reader — `GET /_probe/runs/{id}` read any run's results for ANY authenticated user, no suite-ownership check, mounted in prod; a UUID is not a capability token. Deleted rather than gated, because being a forgotten sibling is precisely how it escaped #989's redaction sweep two PRs earlier, and pinned as a 404 so it cannot creep back. **#727** moved target-shape resolution into `datasources/registry.py`, ending a second dispatch-by-type site that silently falsified the 'adding a datasource is one registry entry' contract (#716 already had to edit both) — now enforced by a test comparing the adapter set against the resolver set, not by a comment asking people to remember. **#905 closed by triage, not by building:** item 1 (beat liveness) shipped in #904 and was verified live today; item 2's stated goal — a wedged reconnect dies rather than hanging — is **met by item 1**, cause-agnostically, which is the property the issue itself argued for. I deliberately did NOT pin broker settings on top: the issue asks to *investigate* why the reconnect loop neither retried nor raised, I cannot establish that without reproducing the wedge, and shipping unverified settings against live prod is a placebo. Item 3 became [#1052](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1052) — workspace-wide `last_polled_at` staleness, the one signal that cannot lie, because every incident in this class is the worker looking alive and writing nothing, so anything derived from its own writes cannot fire when it is what broke. **Harness credentials fixed for #1032:** ACCOUNTADMIN PAT → the terraform provider (it creates account roles; `DATAQ_LOADER` cannot create itself), loader PAT → the KV secret the containers read; both verified by asserting `CURRENT_ROLE()`, not by the write succeeding. The targeted apply propagated it — **5 of the plan's 8 changes**, because a blanket apply would have ARMED both ADF triggers (`activated false -> true`) on a harness meant to be asleep, and silently altered the warehouse via provider drift. All five harness apps verified `Stopped` afterwards.)

(**2026-07-19 — W3 CLOSED: the four build items shipped, wind-down re-homed to W5.** #877 (CI audit gate closed with rationale), #753 → [#927](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/927), #910 → [#930](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/930), #904 → [#931](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/931), #591 → [#932](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/932); #588/#590 re-milestoned to W5 (subscription-lapse timeline, not build readiness). **The reviews were worth more than the features this session** — every one of the four found defects the green test suite did not: the #753 409 was leaking grant-scoped suite names AND `pipeline_runs` was still an unhandled-500 path for every polled orchestration connection; #910's `page` mode shipped as **dead code** while client-side throws reported "503 Service unavailable" over a healthy backend; and #904 — a watchdog written to end silent hangs — had an **unbounded Redis read on the watching thread** (#854 verbatim), a guard that **didn't work** (the non-expiring stamp let a *predecessor's* key arm it → permanent crash loop), and an `os._exit` that would abort a live GX run. All three now go through one new `RangeReader`/`read_range` seam: Parquet answers schema *and* `num_rows` from its footer in a couple of small range GETs whatever the object's size, and CSV takes a bounded head read for its schema and a **streamed** pyarrow scan for its count. A run mixing volume with column-freshness still reads the object exactly once. (**2026-07-25 (later still) — #943 shipped, closing the unbounded-flat-file class.** Batch resolution drained every page under the prefix into a list on **every run**, before the runner was even built — so a landing zone with a long history of dated files grew the retained listing without bound on a scheduled path. The listing is now streamed and folded in a single pass keeping only the running bests, so memory is flat regardless of history. The fold reproduces the previous `max()` calls *exactly*, including their first-wins tie-breaking — pinned by a parametrised equivalence test that recomputes the original formulation, because a `>=` would silently flip every tie. **AC 1 as written ('read a bounded number of pages') was not implementable safely and was deliberately not faked:** both stores list ascending, so the newest key — the one `latest` wants — is precisely what a truncated scan misses, and a capped scan would return a confidently wrong older batch. Instead a generous hard limit *refuses* (`BatchListingTooLargeError`, deliberately not a `BatchNotFoundError`, which would skip the run and report success nightly) and a soft limit logs so the cost is visible before it is an incident. The retention test needed two attempts: the first measured *after* the fold returned, where every local is already dead, so it passed against a full materialisation — it now samples peak retention mid-stream. lines: | **v1 baseline** | `v1.0.0` tagged 2026-07-04 — 187/189 roadmap tasks (~99%); all 8 weekly exit gates met; deployed to Azure Container Apps; retro at [retro-v1.md](retro-v1.md); full ledger at [progress-v1.md](progress-v1.md) |

| **Current cycle** | **v1.1 — 6 weeks + a stretch week, 2026-07-04 → 2026-08-15 (+ W7 stretch to 2026-08-22)** (planned 2026-07-04 from [context/post-v1-roadmap.md](../context/post-v1-roadmap.md)). Sequencing is **subscription-driven**: Weeks 1–3 extract everything that needs the expiring Snowflake (lapses within days) and Azure (~2026-07-25) subscriptions, then wind down gracefully; Weeks 4–6 run the roadmap's recommended opening sequence (Theme-1 `schema_drift` + `anomaly` → scale-aware execution G-b → incident/lineage design G-d — the G-d design half, #596, was pulled forward and done in W3, 2026-07-10) on cloud-independent infra; W7 is the stretch/burn-down buffer. See [Cycle plan](#cycle-plan--v11-6-weeks--stretch-2026-07-04--2026-08-22) below. |

| **Open issues** | **30** in the **`v1.1 Backlog`** milestone (48 open repo-wide — re-counted 2026-08-01 after the v1.1 W5 close-out: the 8 scheduled issues (#568/#349/#424/#351/#593/#594/#283/#345) all closed as PRs #1113–#1122 (all merged 2026-08-01), and #1116's review filed one new one, #1118 (SSRF/exfiltration class on `*_secret_name` connection-test paths); the merge train also filed **#1123** (the #573 CI-flake class recurred — two distinct antd+userEvent tests timed out at 5s on slow runners, one twice) and shipped its fix same-day as **[#1124](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1124)** — `testTimeout` is now CI-gated to 15s in `frontend/vite.config.ts` (local stays 5s so a hung test still fails fast)) — `gh issue list --milestone 'v1.1 Backlog' --state open`; the population is stated here because the figure has silently drifted before, so **re-count it, don't decrement it**. (**2026-07-29 — 29 in the milestone, 54 open repo-wide** — #1111 filed AND fixed same-session; re-counted after #1110 closed #892+#912 and filed #1109, and after Batch 3's first wave — #1103/#1105/#1106 closed #919/#925/#1064 and filed #1104/#1107/#1108 — and after Batch 2 — #1100 closed #1091+#1090+#1052 (verified individually per the first-issue-only rule) and filed #1101/#1102; earlier that day #1096 closed #755 and #1098 closed #1066 — a same-day backlog-burn sweep of ~25 candidate issues against `main` found **zero** close-now issues beyond these: everything else still reproduces, evidence per-issue in the session; earlier the same day #1088/#1089/#1092/#1093/#1094/#1095 — the session filed #1085/#1086/#1087/#1090/#1091 and closed #1085/#1086/#1087/#1072/#1067.) (**2026-07-25 (later) — standing rule added + a self-inflicted register bug found and fixed.** **CONTRIBUTING rule 3a / CLAUDE.md §11: "pre-existing" is not a disposition** (user, this session) — DataQ is in prod, so a defect's age says nothing about its blast radius; every finding ends **fixed or filed**, never noted-in-a-reply or buried in a docstring. Verified-benign is a valid outcome *if the determination is recorded*; unexamined is not. Discharged immediately against my own session: two findings I had documented in code but never filed are now [#989](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/989) (`SafeMonitorError` echoes a target cell value, which its own rule forbids — bounded and arguably justified, but the redaction policy has no say in it) and [#990](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/990) (**model-vs-migration schema parity is never checked anywhere** — the test schema is `create_all`, so #457's guard covers 2 of the 3 predicate spellings, and this same gap is what let #913's mistargeted backfill migration break every fresh database). **The register bug: three PRs claimed 13 issues and closed 3.** GitHub honours only the **first** issue after a `Closes` keyword; the rest of a comma list are ignored **silently**. Ten issues sat open against shipped work — and this repo already recorded the same trap on the #720 batch, which is exactly why knowing it is not enough. All ten closed by hand with their merging PR named; the countermeasure is now structural rather than memorial — the **PR template** carries the one-keyword-per-issue rule *and* the post-merge `gh issue view` verification loop.) (**2026-07-25 — verification sweep + three closing PRs: 89 → 82 open, 15 issues resolved.** Six agents re-checked 48 candidate issues **against the tree, not the ticket** — the discipline that caught #724 the day before. **Closed on evidence, no code needed (6):** #322/#573 (both already fixed, tracked to completion under later duplicates #640/#714 — verified in-tree and re-run), #929 (subset of #787, which now carries a fresh count: **112** sites across 14 files, not the filing-time ~93), #893 (warehouse lineage WAS live-verified on both warehouses in the 07-18 arc; evidence quoted onto the issue), #731 (findings register discharged — 3 of 5 children closed, 2 tracked), #541 (**the audit is the deliverable**: both 500-risk paths are closed — `pipeline_runs` cascades, `suites.connection_id` 409s at the service layer — and the three remaining `users.id` FKs are latent by design, with the revisit trigger recorded on the issue). **Shipped (9):** [#984](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/984) docs/SAST (#729/#730/#800/#806), [#985](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/985) frontend (#915/#916/#949/#563/#601), [#986](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/986) backend (#900/#306/#728/#457). **The reviews were again worth more than the features.** #984's first attempt **broke the SAST gate**: I removed five bandit suppressions after counting *warnings* (37 → 0) instead of the gate's **exit code**, which went 0 → 5 findings. The diagnosis was wrong too — each site had TWO markers, one on the flagged node (load-bearing) and one outside its range (inert), and the `no failed test` warning names the inert one without saying which is which. All five restored, bare; the prose-tokenization half was real and stays fixed (20 warnings gone); the residual 17 are **intrinsic** to a marker on a multi-line node, so #806's "zero warnings" AC was a false premise and is recorded as such. #900's obvious fix (classify everything) was likewise wrong and **six existing tests said so** — it turned "unknown freshness column 'nope'" into "the run failed to execute", so safety is now *declared* via a `SafeMonitorError` marker rather than guessed. Reviewers also caught two places where my own text overclaimed: the #915 comment asserted `last_error`/`degraded_reason` were exclusive (they are not → [#987](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/987)), and the #457 guard's docstring claimed three coverages while checking two (the migration is never applied in the test schema) — both corrected to state the hole rather than imply it is closed. **Two lessons banked:** *judge a suppression by the gate's exit code, never its warning count* (now CONTRIBUTING rule 16), and *a subagent's `git checkout` moves YOUR HEAD* — a background review agent stranded a commit on local `main` mid-session; recovered via reflog + `cherry-pick --no-commit`, and reviewers are now told to stay read-only.) (**2026-07-24 — full open-issue triage (all 89, milestone-independent); three register entries were WRONG, each verified against the tree rather than the ticket.** [#724](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/724) (P1, orchestration-connection delete 500) was **already fixed** — migration `a3b4c5d6e7f8` + `models.py:715` + the regression test at `test_connection_service.py:350` all landed inside [#927](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/927) while addressing #753; closed. [#708](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/708) and [#748](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/748) are the **same issue filed twice** (07-08 from the #605 `runs ADD COLUMN` hang, 07-10 from the #747 `connections` hang); #708 closed into #748, which keeps the fuller record (the orphaned-backend half + the silent-`/healthz` observation), and #748's own first AC is now **partially** ticked — `lock_timeout=15s` shipped on the migrate engine (`alembic/env.py:53`, also #927) but the **bounded retry loop did not**, so a contended migrate still needs a manual retry. [#806](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/806) was **stale, not fixed**: the `_PENALTY` map it points at moved to `services/rollup.py` in the #948 unification, and a fresh `bandit -q -r backend/app` at the CI-pinned 1.9.4 emits **37** warnings, not 3, in two classes — dead suppressions across four files (`rollup.py`, `orchestration/dbt.py`, `dataset_reader.py`, `schema_drift.py`) **plus a class the ticket never described**: bandit tokenizes everything after `# nosec` as test IDs, so our own convention of writing `# nosec B105 — <prose>` emits one warning per word. Harmless to security (unknown tokens are ignored, the suppression never widens) but it is 20 lines of self-inflicted noise on the one gate an operator scans for real findings — the #828 "confident-looking nothing" class applied to SAST output. Re-scoped with the convention fix (reason on its own line above) as an AC. **Standing lesson: a P1 that has silently already been fixed costs the same attention as a real one every time the register is read.** Also re-checked and **still valid**: #601 (`frontend/.prettierignore` has no `e2e-live/.auth/` entry), #728 (the ACA host allowlist is still hardcoded at `mcp/server.py:575`), #730 (the real prod FQDN is still tracked in `CLAUDE.md`, `deploy/README.md`, `backend/tests/mcp/test_mcp_tools.py`), #541 (four FKs still lack `ondelete` — `suites.connection_id` + three `users.id` refs). **[#590](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/590)'s premise is stale and needs re-scoping, not execution:** the subscription reads `Enabled` / `PayAsYouGo` / `spendingLimit: Off`, so there is **no ~07-25 lapse** to race — the wind-down is now purely a cost decision, and until it is taken every awake resource bills real money uncapped. **[#588](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/588) is the one still on a real clock** (Snowflake trial), and #954 already records two dead prod Snowflake PATs — that leg may already be failing every scheduled run into the #419 always-alert path.) (**2026-07-24 — [#980](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/980) filed** from the `bikini/exploitarium` 0-day triage below: a Redis-8 upgrade gate, not a live defect.) (**2026-07-19 — W3 CLOSED: the four build items shipped, wind-down re-homed to W5.** #877 (CI audit gate closed with rationale), #753 → [#927](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/927), #910 → [#930](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/930), #904 → [#931](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/931), #591 → [#932](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/932); #588/#590 re-milestoned to W5 (subscription-lapse timeline, not build readiness). **The reviews were worth more than the features this session** — every one of the four found defects the green test suite did not: the #753 409 was leaking grant-scoped suite names AND `pipeline_runs` was still an unhandled-500 path for every polled orchestration connection; #910's `page` mode shipped as **dead code** while client-side throws reported "503 Service unavailable" over a healthy backend; and #904 — a watchdog written to end silent hangs — had an **unbounded Redis read on the watching thread** (#854 verbatim), a guard that **didn't work** (the non-expiring stamp let a *predecessor's* key arm it → permanent crash loop), and an `os._exit` that would abort a live GX run. All 7 fixed. **Lesson recorded: the watchdog's tests were green on all three logic bugs because every loop test ran ONE iteration against a pre-seeded state — the defects lived in state carried ACROSS iterations.** Two process misses, recorded not buried: I pushed #931 with a failing lint gate (ran ruff, saw "1 fixable", pushed anyway), and a branch switch swept #591's files into the #904 branch (caught when its tests failed on the wrong branch; commits split). Filed en route: [#925](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/925) (browse 200-cap), [#928](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/928) (`/pipeline_runs` has no paging — a loop "counted" 20,200 rows against a 211-row table because every page re-read page 1), [#929](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/929) (endemic assert-with-side-effects in wire tests).**) (**2026-07-18 night (latest) — ADR 0037: the asset access model REVERSED, one day after #920 ([#923](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/923) via [#924](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/924), user-directed).** The #920/#845/#901 identity-redaction regime described in the previous entry is **superseded**: asset identity + lineage topology (incl. column pairs) are now visible to EVERY workspace member; the health rollup is **workspace-true** (aggregated over ALL composing suites — one verdict per asset, byte-identical across viewers, pinned by a wire test); the ADR 0027 grants now guard **suite-derived detail only** (composing-suite names/runs/results/samples/incidents — suite-grain 404-no-leak intact; on the asset page hidden suites collapse to a derived restricted count). All three now go through one new `RangeReader`/`read_range` seam: Parquet answers schema *and* `num_rows` from its footer in a couple of small range GETs whatever the object's size, and CSV takes a bounded head read for its schema and a **streamed** pyarrow scan for its count. A run mixing volume with column-freshness still reads the object exactly once. (**2026-07-25 (later still) — #943 shipped, closing the unbounded-flat-file class.** Batch resolution drained every page under the prefix into a list on **every run**, before the runner was even built — so a landing zone with a long history of dated files grew the retained listing without bound on a scheduled path. The listing is now streamed and folded in a single pass keeping only the running bests, so memory is flat regardless of history. The fold reproduces the previous `max()` calls *exactly*, including their first-wins tie-breaking — pinned by a parametrised equivalence test that recomputes the original formulation, because a `>=` would silently flip every tie. **AC 1 as written ('read a bounded number of pages') was not implementable safely and was deliberately not faked:** both stores list ascending, so the newest key — the one `latest` wants — is precisely what a truncated scan misses, and a capped scan would return a confidently wrong older batch. Instead a generous hard limit *refuses* (`BatchListingTooLargeError`, deliberately not a `BatchNotFoundError`, which would skip the run and report success nightly) and a soft limit logs so the cost is visible before it is an incident. The retention test needed two attempts: the first measured *after* the fold returned, where every local is already dead, so it passed against a full materialisation — it now samples peak retention mid-stream.
